items.item: A slot-bounded parallelism ceiling isn't an arbitrary cluster-sizing inconvenience — it's the same resource-isolation idea the chapter's earlier windowing topics apply to memory, applied here to scheduling: a fixed, countable resource with no soft overflow.

items.item: Operator chaining being configurable rather than automatic in every case matters because a shuffle or an incompatible parallelism setting silently un-chains two operators that look adjacent in the code, which is exactly the kind of invisible cost this topic's measurement makes visible.

items.item: Backpressure needing no explicit signal isn't a design limitation to work around — it's the entire point of credit-based flow control: the slowdown is a structural consequence of credits running out, not a message that could fail to be sent.

at.step: Reveal: backpressure with no explicit signal, by design

items.item: Stating the per-job-mode removal as a currency fact (removed, not merely discouraged) matters because the 1.20 docs branch this topic otherwise cites still describes per-job mode as only deprecated, not gone — the 2.0 release notes are the source that actually confirms removal.

items.item: A single runtime executing both batch and stream jobs isn't a convenience feature bolted onto a streaming engine — it reflects the same unified-model thinking the Dataflow Model paper argued for at the API level, now realized at the execution-engine level.
